errors: put-vs-load race: put does inflight.remove and install() as two separate steps outside one lock, and the loader does inflight.remove(key,mine) then install() also non-atomically; interleaving loader-remove, put-remove, put-install, loader-install lets the older DB value overwrite the put, contradicting the stated guarantee
Small window where a load's inflight.remove precedes its install lets a new miss start a duplicate load
Executor rejection not handled (future never completes until the 2s timeout)
A.note: Clean design with the right decisions, but the put-wins-over-load guarantee is not atomic and can be violated.

errors: Uses Clock.millis (wall clock) for TTL; NTP jumps can expire or resurrect entries early or late
B.note: Future stored in the map plus a TreeSet expiry index under one lock, identity check on completion, completion outside the lock and expired-first eviction: correct and well argued, if long.

errors: Only RuntimeException is caught around the load; an Error leaves the in-flight future registered and never completed, so waiters time out and later gets for that key hit the dead future
C.note: Correct single-flight with the stale-load check done atomically under the lock; a solid, right-sized answer.

errors: Put/invalidate during an in-flight load is not handled in code: the loader's later put overwrites a fresher put and resurrects invalidated keys (acknowledged only as an optional fix)
Waiters use f.join() with no timeout despite the text recommending one; an Error from the loader is not caught, so waiters on that future hang forever
loadExecutor is injected but never used
D.note: Correct intrusive LRU and single-flight, but leaves the stale-load overwrite race open and the code contradicts its own timeout advice.

errors: Waiters join() with no timeout, so a hung DB call pins all waiting threads
Claim that expired entries are the first evicted by LRU is only approximately true
E.note: Map and in-flight registry under one lock make the hit/miss/register decision atomic; short, correct and well reasoned.

errors: No re-check after putIfAbsent, so a miss racing with a just-completed load can start a duplicate load (harmless but avoidable)
Stray 'ponytail:' artifact in the text; 'a few million ops/s on one lock' is an unsupported figure
F.note: Correct expired-first eviction with a lazily compacted heap and atomic put-vs-load check; good tests, slightly noisy write-up.
